subject: Charng et al. (2016)
object: Charng et al. (2016) performed whole-exome sequencing in 31 mostly consanguineous Arab families from Saudi Arabia with neurologic disease, including brain malformations and/or developmental delay/intellectual disability. They proposed 12 novel candidate disease genes, including AAR2, in 11 families. Most variants in candidate genes mapped to regions of absence of heterozygosity and were homozygous. All variants in novel candidate genes were classified as variants of uncertain significance.

subject: Fisher et al. (2025)
object: Fisher et al. (2025) reported 2 sibs born to consanguineous Pakistani parents. Prenatal imaging showed cerebral ventriculomegaly and agenesis of the corpus callosum in both. Autopsies on both sibs showed similar abnormalities, including facial dysmorphism, osteopetrosis, and neuropathologic findings consistent with neuroaxonal dystrophy.

subject: Fisher et al. (2025)
object: In 2 sibs, born to consanguineous Pakistani parents, who had neuroaxonal dystrophy with osteopetrosis, Fisher et al. (2025) used trio exome sequencing to identify a homozygous nonsense variant in exon 3 of the BORCS5 gene (c.283C>T, p.Arg95Ter; NM_058169.4). Each parent was heterozygous for the variant.

subject: Fisher et al. (2025)
object: Fisher et al. (2025) found that 1 of the 2 affected sibs was also homozygous for a missense variant of uncertain significance in the SCYL2 gene (c.902G>A, p.Arg301His; NM_017988.5), for which both parents were heterozygous. Because the autopsy findings in the 2 sibs were identical, the authors raised the possibility that the SCYL2 variant did not contribute to the phenotype.

subject: Fisher et al. (2025)
object: Fisher et al. (2025) noted that neuroaxonal dystrophy with osteopetrosis was first reported in a consanguineous Moroccan Jewish family and that, until their report, no genetic variant had been linked to the disease.
